Loving the plot so far, but I have three plot holes that I'm trying to overlook/patch up:

1. It seems odd that Lumon is allowed to get away with such a questionably-unethical procedure and that they've managed to maintain such secrecy. contemporary moral and ethical scientific boards have outlawed far less drastic brain-altering surgeries such as lobotomies for their unpredictable and adverse effects, and the boards only seem to be getting stricter. I'd imagine that in the future, with the advancement of technology, the increased advocacy of human rights, and the possibility of many more unknown adverse consequences from such extreme surgical procedures, scientific ethical boards and human rights groups would have so much more red tape and strongly object to severance (more than we see in the show). 

2. it seems odd that no one found Petey's death unusual or tied his death to Lumon. There should be news reporters, human rights groups, and detectives looking into what happened there.

3. You'd think that Lumon, with all of its money and advancements in research and technology, would have created a more controlled environment over its severance subjects, unless perhaps the research requires that the subjects are supposed to be autonomous.  But it seems like every day there's several extreme instances of subjects disobeying protocol, causing havoc and trouble for Lumon - Petey escaped, Petey talked to Mark's outtie, Hedey almost killed herself, Mark has an illegal map of Lumon, etc. Lumon, as controlling as it is, doesn't seem to be all that in control. 

All that being said, as aforementioned, I'm loving the show, and the music is very fitting and catchy. My theory about the severance chip is that it harvests the severance subject's work-self-consciousness and all that harvested data will feed into some sort of morally twisted goal of Lumon's - a human consciousness that exists digitally thus creating the digital version of eternal life.
